summary.name: Huxli
summary.one_liner: Huxli is an AI study assistant for students that writes essays, humanizes AI-generated text, turns lectures into notes, and solves math problems with steps.
use_cases: Rewriting AI-generated text to read as human
Turning lecture recordings or PDFs into study notes
Getting step-by-step solutions to math problems
Making flashcards and quizzes for exam prep
summary.what_it_does: Huxli offers four tools: a Humanizer that rewrites text sentence by sentence and states it checks against GPTZero, ZeroGPT, and Turnitin; a Lecture to Notes tool that takes a recording, PDF, or YouTube link and produces notes, flashcards, and quizzes; a Math Solver that accepts typed or photographed problems in algebra, calculus, statistics, and physics and shows the steps; and an Essay Writer that researches, outlines, and drafts sections from a pasted rubric. The page lists three paid tiers, Starter at $7.99/month, Study at $14.99/month, and Study Pack at $22.99/month, with yearly billing at 50% off. Performance claims such as 36% better grades and 97% accurate humanization come from the vendor and are not independently verified.
notable: Humanizer checks output against GPTZero, ZeroGPT, and Turnitin before submission
Lecture to Notes accepts recordings, PDFs, or YouTube links
Math Solver accepts photographed problems and shows work
caveats: Paid subscriptions required for full access; Starter tier limits lecture notes, humanizations, and math tutor usage
Performance and detector-evasion claims are vendor claims and not independently verified
Academic integrity concerns: the page centers on producing full essays and passing AI detectors
